::: {.callout-important}
## 本节考纲要求

本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.8 Integration：

- 把 integration 理解为 reverse differentiation，并积分 $(ax+b)^n$、constant multiples、sums 和 differences；
- 处理 constant of integration；
- 计算 definite integrals，包括简单的 improper integrals；
- 用 definite integration 求由曲线、坐标轴平行直线、直线或两条曲线围成的面积，以及绕坐标轴旋转所得的体积。

下列 19 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干保留原题，只把 PDF 的排版符号整理为 LaTeX；没有改写或编造题目。答案按对应 mark scheme 的得分步骤展开。
:::

## 1. Core knowledge

::: {.formula-panel}
### Reverse differentiation

若 $n\ne -1$，则

$$\int (ax+b)^n\,dx=\frac{(ax+b)^{n+1}}{a(n+1)}+c.$$

特别地，先把每一项写成幂，再逐项积分：

$$\int x^n\,dx=\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+c,\qquad
\int kf(x)\,dx=k\int f(x)\,dx.$$
:::

::: {.study-card}
### Definite integral, area and volume

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=F(b)-F(a).$$

若区域在 $x$ 轴上方，面积为 $\int_a^b y\,dx$；若曲线和直线之间有上下边界，则积分
“upper − lower”。绕 $x$ 轴旋转时使用

$$V=\pi\int_a^b y^2\,dx,$$

若区域不是直接从 $x$ 轴开始，要用外半径平方减内半径平方。绕 $y$ 轴时，可使用

$$V=\pi\int (x_{\rm outer}^2-x_{\rm inner}^2)\,dy.$$
:::

## 2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q01}
### Question 1 · 9709/11/O/N/20 Q2

The equation of a curve is such that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{(x-3)^2}+x$. It is given that the curve passes through the point $(2,7)$. Find the equation of the curve. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Rewrite the derivative as $(x-3)^{-2}+x$ and integrate:

$$y=-\frac{1}{x-3}+\frac{x^2}{2}+c.$$

Use $(2,7)$:

$$7=-\frac1{2-3}+\frac{2^2}{2}+c=1+2+c,$$

so $c=4$. Therefore

$$\boxed{y=-\frac1{x-3}+\frac{x^2}{2}+4}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q01"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_11.pdf, Q2, and matching 9709_w20_ms_11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q02}
### Question 2 · 9709/11/M/J/21 Q1

The equation of a curve is such that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3}{x^4}+32x^3$. It is given that the curve passes through the point $\left(\frac12,4\right)$. Find the equation of the curve. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Integrate both terms:

$$y=\int\left(3x^{-4}+32x^3\right)\,dx
=-x^{-3}+8x^4+c.$$

Substitute $x=\frac12$, $y=4$:

$$4=-\left(\frac12\right)^{-3}+8\left(\frac12\right)^4+c
=-8+\frac12+c.$$

Thus $c=\frac{23}{2}$, hence

$$\boxed{y=-\frac1{x^3}+8x^4+\frac{23}{2}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q02"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_11.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_s21_ms_11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q03}
### Question 3 · 9709/12/O/N/21 Q4

A curve is such that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{8}{(3x+2)^2}$. The curve passes through the point $\left(2,5\frac23\right)$. Find the equation of the curve. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

$$\frac{dy}{dx}=8(3x+2)^{-2}.$$

Integrating, with $u=3x+2$ and $du=3\,dx$,

$$y=-\frac{8}{3(3x+2)}+c.$$

Use $\left(2,5\frac23\right)$:

$$5\frac23=-\frac{8}{3(8)}+c=-\frac13+c,$$

so $c=6$. Thus

$$\boxed{y=-\frac{8}{3(3x+2)}+6}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q03"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_12.pdf, Q4, and matching 9709_w21_ms_12.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q04}
### Question 4 · 9709/12/O/N/22 Q8(a)

The equation of a curve is such that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^{1/2}-3x^{-1/2}$. The curve passes through the point $(3,5)$. Find the equation of the curve. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

$$y=\int\left(3x^{1/2}-3x^{-1/2}\right)\,dx
=2x^{3/2}-6x^{1/2}+c.$$

Substitute $(3,5)$:

$$5=2(3)^{3/2}-6(3)^{1/2}+c=6\sqrt3-6\sqrt3+c,$$

so $c=5$. Therefore

$$\boxed{y=2x^{3/2}-6x^{1/2}+5}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q04"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_12.pdf, Q8(a), and matching 9709_w22_ms_12.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q05}
### Question 5 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q10(a–b)

At the point $(4,-1)$ on a curve, the gradient of the curve is $-\frac32$. It is given that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{-1/2}+k$, where $k$ is a constant. (a) Show that $k=-2$. (b) Find the equation of the curve. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

(a) At $x=4$,

$$-\frac32=4^{-1/2}+k=\frac12+k,$$

so

$$\boxed{k=-2}.$$

(b) Now $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{-1/2}-2$. Integrate:

$$y=2x^{1/2}-2x+c.$$

Use $(4,-1)$:

$$-1=2(4)^{1/2}-2(4)+c=4-8+c,$$

so $c=3$. Hence

$$\boxed{y=2\sqrt{x}-2x+3}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q05"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf, Q10(a–b), and matching 9709_m23_ms_12.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q06}
### Question 6 · 9709/11/M/J/21 Q11(d)

The equation of a curve is $y=2(3x+4)^{1/2}-x$. Find the exact area of the region bounded by the curve, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=4$. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

The required area is

$$A=\int_0^4\left[2(3x+4)^{1/2}-x\right]\,dx.$$

Integrating term by term:

$$A=\left[\frac49(3x+4)^{3/2}-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4.$$

Therefore

$$A=\left(\frac49\cdot16^{3/2}-8\right)-\frac49\cdot4^{3/2}
=\left(\frac{256}{9}-8\right)-\frac{32}{9}
=\boxed{\frac{152}{9}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q06"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_11.pdf, Q11(d), and matching 9709_s21_ms_11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q07}
### Question 7 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q8(a)

The diagram shows part of the curve $y=\dfrac6x$. The points $(1,6)$ and $(3,2)$ lie on the curve. The shaded region is bounded by the curve and the lines $y=2$ and $x=1$. Find the volume generated when the shaded region is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $y$-axis. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Use horizontal washers. For $2\le y\le6$, the outer radius is $x=6/y$ and the inner radius is $x=1$:

$$V=\pi\int_2^6\left[\left(\frac6y\right)^2-1^2\right]\,dy.$$

$$V=\pi\left[-\frac{36}{y}-y\right]_2^6
=\pi\left[(-6-6)-(-18-2)\right]
=\boxed{8\pi}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q07"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q8(a), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q08}
### Question 8 · 9709/11/M/J/20 Q11(b)

The diagram shows part of the curve $y=\dfrac8{x+2}$ and the line $2y+x=8$, intersecting at $A$ and $B$. Find the volume generated when the shaded region, bounded by the curve and the line, is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

From the intersections, the limits are $x=0$ and $x=6$. The line is

$$y=4-\frac{x}{2}.$$

Volume under the line:

$$V_{\rm line}=\pi\int_0^6\left(4-\frac{x}{2}\right)^2dx
=\pi\left[-\frac{x^3}{12}+2x^2-16x\right]_0^6
=42\pi.$$

Volume under the curve:

$$V_{\rm curve}=\pi\int_0^6\left(\frac8{x+2}\right)^2dx
=\pi\left[-\frac{64}{x+2}\right]_0^6
=24\pi.$$

The required volume is their difference:

$$\boxed{V=42\pi-24\pi=18\pi}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q08"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-11.pdf, Q11(b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q09}
### Question 9 · 9709/12/M/J/21 Q9

The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y^2=x-2$ and the lines $x=5$ and $y=1$. The shaded region enclosed by the curve and the lines is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. Find the volume obtained. **[6]**

![Independent vector extraction from the original PDF](/Users/xiesj/Documents/ALevel_Course/CIE_Mathematics/Mathematics_Study/assets/questions/extracted/paper1-integration/9709_s21_p12_q9.svg)

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

The curve meets $y=1$ at $x=3$, because $1^2=x-2$. The volume under the curve from $x=3$ to $x=5$ is

$$\pi\int_3^5 y^2\,dx=\pi\int_3^5(x-2)\,dx
=\pi\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-2x\right]_3^5=4\pi.$$

The part below $y=1$ is a cylinder of volume

$$\pi(1)^2(5-3)=2\pi.$$

Hence the shaded volume is

$$\boxed{4\pi-2\pi=2\pi}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q09"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_12.pdf, Q9, and matching 9709_s21_ms_12.pdf. Diagram independently extracted as vector SVG; it is not a screenshot.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q10}
### Question 10 · 9709/11/O/N/21 Q10(a)

Find $\displaystyle\int_1^\infty\dfrac{1}{(3x-2)^{3/2}}\,dx$. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Write the integrand as $(3x-2)^{-3/2}$:

$$\int(3x-2)^{-3/2}\,dx
=-\frac23(3x-2)^{-1/2}.$$

Apply the improper limit:

$$\int_1^\infty\frac{dx}{(3x-2)^{3/2}}
=\left[-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3x-2}}\right]_1^\infty
=0-\left(-\frac23\right)
=\boxed{\frac23}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q10"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_11.pdf, Q10(a), and matching 9709_w21_ms_11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q11}
### Question 11 · 9709/11/O/N/21 Q10(b)

The diagram shows the curve with equation $y=\dfrac{1}{(3x-2)^{3/2}}$. The shaded region is bounded by the curve, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=1$ and $x=2$. The shaded region is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of revolution. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Since $y^2=(3x-2)^{-3}$,

$$V=\pi\int_1^2(3x-2)^{-3}\,dx.$$

Integrate:

$$V=\pi\left[-\frac{1}{6}(3x-2)^{-2}\right]_1^2
=\pi\left(-\frac1{96}+\frac16\right)
=\boxed{\frac{5\pi}{32}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q11"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_11.pdf, Q10(b), and matching 9709_w21_ms_11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q12}
### Question 12 · 9709/11/M/J/22 Q7(b)

The diagram shows the curve $y=(3x-2)^{1/2}$ and the line $y=\frac12x+1$. The curve and the line intersect at points $A$ and $B$. Hence find the area of the region enclosed between the curve and the line. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

The intersections satisfy

$$\sqrt{3x-2}=\frac{x}{2}+1.$$

The two intersection $x$-coordinates are $x=2$ and $x=6$. On this interval the curve is above the line, so

$$A=\int_2^6\left[(3x-2)^{1/2}-\left(\frac{x}{2}+1\right)\right]dx.$$

Thus

$$A=\left[\frac29(3x-2)^{3/2}-\frac{x^2}{4}-x\right]_2^6
=\frac49.$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{A=\frac49}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q12"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_11.pdf, Q7(b), and matching 9709_s22_ms_11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q13}
### Question 13 · 9709/11/M/J/23 Q10(a)

The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y=\dfrac{4}{(2x-1)^2}$ and parts of the lines $x=1$ and $y=1$. The curve passes through the points $A(1,4)$ and $B\left(\frac32,1\right)$. Find the exact volume generated when the shaded region is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

For $1\le x\le\frac32$, the volume under the curve is

$$V_{\rm curve}=\pi\int_1^{3/2}\frac{16}{(2x-1)^4}\,dx
=\pi\left[-\frac{8}{3(2x-1)^3}\right]_1^{3/2}
=\frac{7\pi}{3}.$$

The region below $y=1$ is a cylinder of volume

$$V_{\rm cylinder}=\pi\cdot1^2\cdot\left(\frac32-1\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{V=\frac{7\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{11\pi}{6}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q13"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_11.pdf, Q10(a), and matching 9709_s23_ms_11.pdf.</div>

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q14}
### Question 14 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q11(b)

The diagram shows the curve with equation $x=y^2+1$. The points $A(5,2)$ and $B(2,-1)$ lie on the curve. Find the volume of revolution when the region between the curve and the line $AB$ is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $y$-axis. **[9]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

The gradient of $AB$ is $1$, so its equation is

$$y=x-3,\qquad\text{or}\qquad x=y+3.$$

Using horizontal washers about the $y$-axis:

For the curve, $x=y^2+1$, so

$$V_{\rm curve}=\pi\int_{-1}^2(y^2+1)^2\,dy
=\pi\left[\frac{y^5}{5}+\frac{2y^3}{3}+y\right]_{-1}^2
=\frac{78\pi}{5}.$$

For the line, $x=y+3$, so

$$V_{\rm line}=\pi\int_{-1}^2(y+3)^2\,dy=39\pi.$$

Subtracting gives

$$\boxed{V=39\pi-\frac{78\pi}{5}=\frac{117\pi}{5}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q14"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf, Q11(b), and matching 9709_m23_ms_12.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q15}
### Question 15 · 9709/11/M/J/24 Q9

The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y=\dfrac{1}{(5x-4)^{1/3}}$ and the lines $x=2.4$ and $y=1$. The curve intersects the line $y=1$ at the point $(1,1)$. Find the exact volume of the solid generated when the shaded region is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. **[6]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

The curve meets $y=1$ at $x=1$, and $2.4=\frac{12}{5}$. Since $y^2=(5x-4)^{-2/3}$,

$$V_{\rm curve}=\pi\int_1^{12/5}(5x-4)^{-2/3}\,dx
=\pi\left[\frac{3}{5}(5x-4)^{1/3}\right]_1^{12/5}
=\frac{3\pi}{5}.$$

The cylinder below $y=1$ has volume

$$V_{\rm cylinder}=\pi\cdot1^2\left(\frac{12}{5}-1\right)=\frac{7\pi}{5}.$$

The shaded region is between the line $y=1$ and the curve, so

$$\boxed{V=V_{\rm cylinder}-V_{\rm curve}
=\frac{7\pi}{5}-\frac{3\pi}{5}
=\frac{4\pi}{5}}.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q15"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q9, and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf.</div>
:::

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q16}
### Question 16 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q9(b)

The diagram shows the curve with equation $y=(2x^3+10)^{1/2}$. The region shaded in the diagram is enclosed by the curve and the straight lines $x=1$, $x=3$ and $y=0$. Find the volume of the solid obtained when the shaded region is rotated through $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. **[3]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Because $y^2=2x^3+10$,

$$V=\pi\int_1^3 y^2\,dx
=\pi\int_1^3(2x^3+10)\,dx.$$

Therefore

$$V=\pi\left[\frac{x^4}{2}+10x\right]_1^3
=\pi\left(\frac{81}{2}+30-\frac12-10\right)
=\boxed{60\pi}.$$
</details>

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q17}
### Question 17 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q5(b)

The equation of a curve is such that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=4x-3x^{1/2}+1$. Given that the curve passes through the point $(4,11)$, find the equation of the curve. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Integrate:

$$y=\int(4x-3x^{1/2}+1)\,dx
=2x^2-2x^{3/2}+x+c.$$

Use $(4,11)$:

$$11=2(4)^2-2(4)^{3/2}+4+c=32-16+4+c=20+c.$$

Hence $c=-9$, and

$$\boxed{y=2x^2-2x^{3/2}+x-9}.$$
</details>

:::

### Question 18 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q7(b)

The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y=\dfrac{12}{(2x+1)^{1/3}}$. The point $A$ on the curve has coordinates $\left(\frac72,6\right)$. Find the area of the region bounded by the curve and the lines $x=0$, $x=\frac72$ and $y=0$. **[4]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

The required area is

$$A=\int_0^{7/2}12(2x+1)^{-1/3}\,dx.$$

An antiderivative is $9(2x+1)^{2/3}$, so

$$A=\left[9(2x+1)^{2/3}\right]_0^{7/2}
=9\left(8^{2/3}-1\right)
=9(4-1)
=\boxed{27}.$$
</details>

::: {.question-card #p1-int-q19}
### Question 19 · 9709/12/O/N/24 Q7(b)

The diagram shows part of the curve with equation $y=-2x^2+8x+11$ and the line with equation $y=8x+9$. Find the area of the shaded region. **[5]**

<details class="answer-panel"><summary>Show detailed mark scheme answer</summary>

Find the intersections:

$$-2x^2+8x+11=8x+9
\Longrightarrow -2x^2+2=0
\Longrightarrow x=\pm1.$$

The curve is above the line between $x=-1$ and $x=1$. Therefore

$$A=\int_{-1}^{1}\left[(-2x^2+8x+11)-(8x+9)\right]dx
=\int_{-1}^{1}(2-2x^2)\,dx.$$

Hence

$$A=\left[2x-\frac23x^3\right]_{-1}^{1}
=\boxed{\frac83}\approx2.67.$$
</details>
<label class="done-toggle"><input type="checkbox" data-progress="p1-int-q19"> Completed</label>
<div class="source-line"><strong>Source:</strong> PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q7(b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf.</div>

## 3. Checklist

- [ ] 能逐项 reverse differentiate，并正确保留 $+c$。
- [ ] 能使用给定点求 constant of integration。
- [ ] 能处理上下限、improper integral 和无限上限。
- [ ] 能区分 area between curves、washers、shell-style horizontal slices。
- [ ] 绕坐标轴旋转时能先确定外半径、内半径，再写 $\pi\int(R^2-r^2)\,dx$ 或 $\pi\int(R^2-r^2)\,dy$。
